title: Automated Runbooks: Private VPC Health Check Failures (Terraform modules & Remediation)
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
Provide a set of operational runbooks and automated remediation playbooks for the most common Private (VPC) deployment health check failures. Deliverables include: curated runbooks for oncall, Terraform module patterns and fixes, small operator-safe automation (SSM/Lambda) to perform guarded remediations, and tests to validate automation against a staging VPC.

Goal:
1) Reduce time-to-recovery for recurring Private health failures by >50% for common failure classes.
2) Provide idempotent, auditable automated remediation flows that can be enabled per-customer or globally.
3) Ship Terraform module knobs and documented runbook steps so SRE/SE teams can apply fixes safely.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Runbooks + automated remediation for: network ACL / SG misconfigurations, NAT gateway failure / route misconfig, kubelet / node agent healthcheck failures, certificate expiry or rotation failures, IAM/service-account permission regressions, and control-plane endpoint connectivity issues.
- Terraform module guidance and example fixes.
- Integration points: PagerDuty escalation, Redwood Console alerts, CloudWatch/Datadog monitors, SSM Automation or Lambda remediation.

Out of scope (for follow-ups):
- Full multi-region disaster recovery runbook (separate ticket).
- Customer-specific managed remediation agreements and billing.

Failure classes, detection signals, and severity mapping:
1) Network misconfig (ACL/SG) — detection: failing healthcheck probes, connection resets in alb/nginx logs, template "healthcheck: 502/connection refused". Severity: high if >5% requests fail, medium otherwise.
2) NAT/egress failure — detection: nodes unable to pull images, control-plane certificate rotation jobs timeout, long tail of 429/5xx to external services. Severity: high for bootstrap failures.
3) Node agent (kubelet/containerd) — detection: node becomes NotReady, kubelet logs show eviction or certificate errors, kube-proxy metrics drop. Severity: medium/high.
4) Control-plane connectivity — detection: API timeouts (kube-apiserver), control-plane healthcheck failing from control-plane monitor. Severity: high.
5) IAM / permission regressions — detection: 403s in controller logs, failed webhook calls or secret fetch failures. Severity: medium.
6) Certificate expiry / TLS misconfiguration — detection: TLS handshake failures for internal endpoints, expired cert observed in secrets manager or certwatch alert. Severity: high.

For each failure class the runbook includes: detection, impact assessment, immediate mitigation, remediation via Terraform (in-place), automated remediation candidate, verification steps, rollback and post-incident actions.

Representative runbook excerpts (concise):
A) Network ACL / Security Group blocking control-plane healthchecks
- Detection: Datadog monitor "private.vpc.health.http_5xx" firing; sample log: "x.x.x.x - - \"GET /healthz\" 403"
- Immediate mitigation: add temporary SG rule to allow source IP range of health probes:
  aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0123456789abcd --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.0.0/16 --description "temp: allow health probes"
- Terraform fix (preferred): in our module (module.private_vpc.security_groups) add explicit rule and plan/apply:
  cd infra/private-vpc
  terraform workspace select staging
  terraform plan -target=module.private_vpc.aws_security_group_rule.health_probe_allow
  terraform apply -target=module.private_vpc.aws_security_group_rule.health_probe_allow -auto-approve
- Automated remediation candidate: SSM Automation document that runs the aws cli command to add rule, tags the change with "auto-remediate:network-health-2026", and triggers a ticket webhook. This automation must require k/v rollback token to remove the rule after 1 hour.
- Verification: wait for health monitor to clear; curl from inside VPC to /healthz and confirm 200. If not recovered, escalate to network eng and revert automation.

B) NAT Gateway / Route table mis-route causing egress failure
- Detection: image pull failures in kubelet: "failed to pull image: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": net/http: request canceled"
- Immediate mitigation: create temporary route to an alternative NAT or enable NAT gateway fallback variable in Terraform: module.private_vpc.nat_gateway_fallback = true
- Terraform remediation (preferred):
  terraform plan -target=module.private_vpc.aws_route.route_to_nat
  terraform apply -target=module.private_vpc.aws_route.route_to_nat -auto-approve
- Automated remediation candidate: Lambda (has least privilege IAM) that checks route table association, and if NAT gateway status != available, re-associates route to backup NAT or spins up elastic IP + small NAT instance (only when module.nat_gateway_autocreate = true). Audit with CloudTrail and post-change ticket.
- Verification: try docker pull within a node (kubectl run -it --rm busybox --image=busybox -- sh -c "wget -qO- https://httpbin.org/get"); verify success.

C) Node agent/kubelet unhealthy due to cert or disk pressure
- Detection: node status NotReady, kubelet logs show "x509: certificate has expired" or "Eviction threshold met"
- Immediate mitigation: cordon node and move workloads:
  kubectl cordon ip-10-0-3-42.us-west-2.compute.internal
  kubectl drain ip-10-0-3-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Terraform remediation (if infra issue): run module.private_nodes.recreate_node for failing ASG instance or use terraform apply to rotate node image. Example:
  terraform apply -target=module.private_nodes.aws_launch_configuration.node_lc -var 'node_recreate=true' -auto-approve
- Automated remediation candidate: An operator runbook that performs a controlled reboot of instance via SSM and reboots kubelet; if reboot fails, create replacement instance via the ASG lifecycle hook.
- Verification: node returns Ready, pods reschedule, podReady metric restored.

Automation design and safety constraints:
- All automated remediation actions MUST be idempotent, rate-limited, and auditable. Each change must create an entry in our incident-change log (POST to internal change API) and emit a CloudTrail/Datadog event.
- For any network/route change, automation must create a temporary allow-list rule with TTL (1 hour), and also enqueue a follow-up Terraform change for a permanent fix.
- Automations will initially be deployed to a read-only mode (dry-run) for 7 days; operator can promote to active remediation via a single feature flag per environment: feature_flag.private_auto_remediate=true.
- Least privilege: Lambdas/SSM documents run with dedicated IAM roles limited to required actions; keys for terraform apply are restricted and require human confirmation unless flagged for low-risk actions (e.g., add SG rule).

Terraform module conventions and examples:
- Expose small "heal" targets so we can apply minimal changes without touching unrelated resources. For example, create resources with logical names that can be targeted: aws_security_group_rule.health_probe_allow, aws_route.route_to_nat, aws_eip.nat_backup.
- Add variables to enable fallback behaviors: nat_gateway_fallback (bool), nat_gateway_autocreate (bool), health_probe_cidr_list (list(string)).
- Provide documented plan/apply commands in runbook to scope changes rather than running full apply. Example module snippet in module.private_vpc/main.tf:
  resource "aws_security_group_rule" "health_probe_allow" {
    type        = "ingress"
    from_port   = 443
    to_port     = 443
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = var.health_probe_cidr_list
    security_group_id = aws_security_group.control_plane.id
  }

- Add outputs that automation can query: output "health_probe_sg_rule_id" { value = aws_security_group_rule.health_probe_allow.id }
Automated remediation implementation options (recommendation):
1) SSM Automation documents for simple CLI-driven fixes (add SG rule, reboot instance, run terraform apply -target). Good for lowest blast radius.
2) Lambda driven orchestrator for multi-step repairs that require state logic (check NAT status -> re-route -> notify). Must be idempotent and tag changes with incident id.
3) Terraform apply from CI runner for permanent fixes (requires gated approval unless tagged low-risk).

Verification and testing plan:
- Create a staging VPC skeleton and inject each failure (test harness):
  - Block SG rule and verify SSM automation adds rule and health clears.
  - Simulate NAT gateway down (mock by disassociating route) and verify Lambda re-route.
- Create automated tests in our infra-ci pipeline that run the remediation in dry-run and assert the expected API calls are issued.
- Canary automations in one non-prod tenant for 14 days, record MTTR and false-positive rate.

Monitoring, alerting and PagerDuty playbook:
- Datadog monitors to detect degraded health (thresholds + sustained duration: e.g., 5m above threshold triggers P1 if high impact).
- Alerts should include remediation suggestion and a one-click link to run the SSM doc (via console button).
- PagerDuty response steps: on P1, run the appropriate SSM automation (link in alert) and assign oncall. If automation fails or is disabled, escalate to network/SRE team.

Post-incident actions and metrics:
- For every automated remediation triggered, require a follow-up ticket to (a) convert the temp fix to Terraform-managed permanent fix, and (b) update the runbook if needed.
- Track metrics: automations_triggered, automations_success_rate, average_time_to_repair_by_class. Target: automations_success_rate >= 90% after canary.

Documentation and handoffs:
- Add these runbooks to Confluence: "Private VPC Runbooks / Automated Remediation" with clear links to Terraform modules in repo infra/private-vpc.
- Provide a short runbook cheat-sheet for oncall containing quick commands (aws cli/ssm/kubectl) and PagerDuty escalation matrix.

Acceptance criteria (done when):
- Runbooks for the six failure classes written and reviewed by Network and SRE (docs link).
- At least two automated remediations implemented (SSM + Lambda), deployed to staging, verified in dry-run, and can be toggled on via feature flag.
- Terraform module changes merged that add minimal heal targets and variables described above.
- Canary run in one staging tenant for 14 days with metrics captured and success rate >= 80% before broader rollout.
